p.src: Now it happened that Elder Zhizhen of Mount Wutai was a living Buddha of his age during the former Song dynasty, able to know the affairs of past and future. Several years earlier, he had already known that Lu Zhishen was one who would transcend the body and comprehend his destiny; only his worldly ties were not yet exhausted, and he still had a debt of bloodshed to repay, so the elder had sent him to make this journey through the mortal world. His innate spiritual roots remained, and the heart of the Way was still within him; now the thought arose in him to come and practise meditation and pay homage to his first master. Song Gongming had likewise always possessed a benevolent heart, and therefore wished to accompany Lu Zhishen in visiting Elder Zhizhen.

u.src: Now it happened that Elder Zhizhen of Mount Wutai was a living Buddha of his age during the former Song dynasty, able to know the affairs of past and future.

Several years earlier, he had already known that Lu Zhishen was one who would transcend the body and comprehend his destiny; only his worldly ties were not yet exhausted, and he still had a debt of bloodshed to repay, so the elder had sent him to make this journey through the mortal world.
His innate spiritual roots remained, and the heart of the Way was still within him; now the thought arose in him to come and practise meditation and pay homage to his first master.
Song Gongming had likewise always possessed a benevolent heart, and therefore wished to accompany Lu Zhishen in visiting Elder Zhizhen.

p.src: Song Jiang and the generals took only their attendants and escorting troops and came with Lu Zhishen to the foot of Mount Wutai. There they pitched camp and first sent a man up the mountain to announce their arrival. Song Jiang and all the brothers removed their armour and customary weapons, changed into ordinary clothes, and climbed the mountain on foot. As they turned towards the outer mountain gate, they heard bells and drums sounding within the monastery. The monks came out to welcome them and advanced to exchange salutations with Song Jiang, Lu Zhishen, and the others. Many among them recognized Lu Zhishen; and when they saw so many leaders, all in perfect order, following Song Jiang, they were astonished. The chief monk of the Dharma hall reported to Song Jiang, “The elder has entered meditative absorption and cannot come to receive you. General, pray do not take offence.” He then invited Song Jiang and the others to sit awhile in the guest quarters. After tea had been served, an attendant came out and announced, “The elder has just emerged from meditation and is waiting especially for you in his abbot’s quarters. The general is invited to enter.” Song Jiang’s company, more than a hundred strong, proceeded directly to the abbot’s quarters to pay their respects to Elder Zhizhen. The elder hurried down the steps to receive them and invited them into the upper hall. When all had exchanged salutations, Song Jiang observed that the monk was over sixty, with eyebrows and hair entirely white, and a rare and ethereal bearing, looking indeed like the image of the holy monk of Fangguang on Mount Tiantai emerging from seclusion. They entered the abbot’s quarters, where Song Jiang invited Elder Zhizhen to take the honoured seat, then burned incense and bowed in worship. After all the generals in the company had bowed, Lu Zhishen stepped forward, placed incense in the burner, and paid homage. Elder Zhizhen said, “Disciple, you have been gone for several years. Murder and arson cannot have been easy work.” Lu Zhishen remained silent and said nothing. Song Jiang stepped forward and said, “I have long heard of Your Reverence’s pure virtue, but alas, my worldly affinity was too slight, and I had no means of beholding your honoured countenance. Now, having come here under imperial command to defeat the Liao, I have been able to pay my respects to the venerable abbot—a supreme blessing in my life. Though our brother Zhishen has killed men and set fires, his loyal heart has never harmed the innocent. Today he has brought Song Jiang and all these brothers to pay homage to the great master.” Elder Zhizhen replied, “Eminent monks often come here, and at leisure we have sometimes discussed the affairs of the world. I have long heard that the general upholds the Way on Heaven’s behalf, with loyalty and righteousness rooted in his heart. With my disciple Zhishen following the general, how could anything go amiss?” Song Jiang thanked him repeatedly.

p.src: Lu Zhishen brought out a bundle of gold, silver, and coloured silks and offered it to his master. Elder Zhizhen said, “My disciple, where did you obtain these things? If they are wealth unrighteously gained, I certainly dare not accept them.” Zhishen replied, “These are things your disciple accumulated from rewards for repeated services. I have no use for them and have brought them especially as an offering to my master, for the monastery’s common expenses.” The elder said, “Even the community would find it difficult to consume such an offering. I shall use it to procure a complete Buddhist canon for you, that your sins may be extinguished and you may soon attain the blessed fruit.” Lu Zhishen bowed and gave thanks. Song Jiang likewise presented gold, silver, and coloured silks to Elder Zhizhen, but the elder firmly refused them. Song Jiang said, “If my master will not accept them, then let the monastery’s bursar use them to prepare a vegetarian feast as an offering to all the monks of this temple.” That day they stayed overnight in the monastery on Mount Wutai, and the elder entertained them with a vegetarian feast; of this there is no need to say more.

p.src: The next day, when the bursar had completed preparations for the feast, bells and drums sounded in the Dharma hall of the Mount Wutai monastery. Elder Zhizhen assembled all the monks there to expound the Dharma and inquire into Zen. Presently all the monks of the monastery, each wearing his kasaya and carrying his sitting cloth, entered the Dharma hall and took their seats. Song Jiang, Lu Zhishen, and all the other leaders stood on either side. At the chime of the guiding bell, two red-gauze lanterns led the elder up to the Dharma seat. Having reached the Dharma seat, Elder Zhizhen first twisted a stick of ceremonial incense and prayed: “With this stick of incense, I humbly pray that His Majesty’s sacred life may equal Heaven’s and that the myriad people may rejoice in their callings; Twisting another stick of ceremonial incense, I pray that today’s patrons of the feast may enjoy peace in body and mind and that their allotted years may be prolonged; And twisting yet another stick of ceremonial incense, I pray that the realm may be secure and the people at peace, that harvests may be abundant and the years harmonious, that the Three Teachings may flourish, and that all four quarters may be tranquil.” When he had finished the prayers, he seated himself upon the Dharma seat. The monks on both sides completed their salutation, then once more stood in attendance. Song Jiang stepped forward, twisted incense between his fingers, and bowed. Then, approaching with palms joined, he inquired into Zen: “I have a word to ask my master: time in this floating world is finite, but the sea of suffering has no shore; the human body is most insignificant, yet birth and death are matters of the utmost gravity.” Elder Zhizhen at once answered with this gatha:

p.src: When he had finished writing, he handed it to Song Jiang and said, “This concerns the affairs of your whole life. Keep it hidden and treasured; in time it will surely be fulfilled.” Song Jiang read it but could not understand its meaning. p.src: Lu Zhishen bowed and received the gatha. After reading it several times, he put it away upon his person and bowed his thanks to his master. They rested there for another night. The next day, Song Jiang, Lu Zhishen, Wu Yong, and the other leaders took leave of the elder and descended the mountain. As they emerged from the monastery, Elder Zhizhen and all the monks accompanied them beyond the mountain gate and bade them farewell.

p.src: Leaving the elder and monks to return to their monastery, let us speak instead of Song Jiang and the generals. They descended to the foot of Mount Wutai, set their troops in motion, and hurried back with the speed of sparks. When the generals returned to the army, Lu Junyi, Gongsun Sheng, and the others came to receive Song Jiang and his company, and they all exchanged greetings. Song Jiang told Lu Junyi and the others how everyone had inquired into Zen and sworn an oath on Mount Wutai. He brought out the Zen verses and showed them to Lu Junyi and Gongsun Sheng, but neither could understand their meaning. Xiao Rang said, “How could the mysteries and Dharma words of Zen be readily understood?” They were all filled with unending astonishment.

p.src: Song Jiang issued orders to hurry the army on its way. The commanders received the order, mustered the entire army, and set out for the Eastern Capital. Wherever they passed, the soldiers took so much as not a single autumn hair from the people. The people came out, supporting the old and leading the young, to behold the imperial army. Seeing what heroes Song Jiang and his commanders were, every one of them sang their praises and admired them. After Song Jiang and his men had travelled for several days, they reached a place called Shuanglin Town. The townspeople and several farmers from nearby villages all crowded round to watch. Song Jiang and his sworn brothers rode in pairs, ranged like a flight of wild geese. As they went, a leader in the vanguard suddenly rolled from his saddle, ran into the crowd watching on the left, seized a man, and cried, “Elder brother, how do you come to be here?” The two exchanged courtesies and began to talk. p.src: His twin pupils shone brightly; his brows spread like the character eight. He stood about seven feet tall, with a three-pronged moustache covering his mouth. He wore a black crinkled-gauze headscarf drawn low over his brows and a brown cloth Taoist robe edged in black. A multicoloured Lü Gong cord girded his waist, and square-toed blue cloth shoes were on his feet. No commonplace mediocrity was he, but surely a recluse of the mountains and forests.

p.src: Seeing the man’s uncommon appearance and his refined, untroubled bearing, Song Jiang hurriedly dismounted, bowed, and said, “May I ask the honoured recluse’s illustrious name?” The man bowed to Song Jiang and said, “I have long heard your renowned name! Today I have at last been granted an audience with you.” Flustered, Song Jiang hastened to return the bow and helped him up, saying, “I am merely Song Jiang; you need not honour me so.” The man said, “My surname is Xu and my given name Guanzhong. My ancestral home is Daming Prefecture, though I now dwell in the wilds. In former days General Yan and I were close friends, but after we parted, more than ten years passed without our meeting again. Later, while travelling the rivers and lakes, I heard that Brother Xiao Yi was serving under your command, and my admiration knew no bounds. Now I heard that you had defeated Liao and were returning in triumph, so I came here especially to behold you. To have seen all you heroes is the good fortune of my life. I should like to invite Brother Yan to my humble dwelling for a brief talk. I wonder whether the general will permit him to go?” Yan Qing also reported, “Brother Xu and I have long been parted, and I never expected to meet him here. Since Brother Xu has shown me such gracious regard, I ought to visit him. Elder brother, go on ahead with the commanders; I shall catch up afterward.” Song Jiang suddenly remembered and said, “Brother Yan Qing often spoke of your heroic spirit and loyal heart. I only lamented that my fortunes were too meagre for us ever to meet. Now that you have favoured me with your regard, may I venture to invite you to come with us and instruct me?” Xu Guanzhong declined with thanks, saying, “Your generosity, loyalty, and righteousness have long made me wish to serve at your side. But my mother is past seventy, and I dare not travel far from her.” Song Jiang said, “If that is so, I would not presume to press you.” Then he said to Yan Qing, “Brother, be sure to return promptly, lest I remain anxious about you. Besides, once we reach the capital, we may be summoned to court at any moment.” Yan Qing said, “I would never dare disobey my elder brother’s command.” He went to inform Lu Junyi as well, and the two parties took their leave of each other. When Song Jiang mounted again, the leaders ahead were already an arrow’s flight away. Seeing him talking with Guanzhong, they had all reined in their horses to wait. Song Jiang thereupon spurred forward and continued on with the commanders.

p.src: The tale now divides into two. Let us tell how Yan Qing summoned a soldier of his personal retinue, had the baggage tied up, and prepared another horse, while yielding his own fine steed to Xu Guanzhong. At an inn farther along, he removed his armour and customary accoutrements and changed into the everyday clothes he carried with him. The two mounted their horses, and the soldier followed behind carrying the bundle. Leaving Shuanglin Town, they took a minor road northwestward. After passing some village houses, woods, and ridges, they came to a remote, winding mountain road. The two spoke of their old friendship and poured out their hearts to each other. Emerging from the secluded mountain path, they rounded a broad stream. After travelling a little over thirty li, Xu Guanzhong pointed and said, “My humble dwelling lies within those lofty mountains over there.” They travelled another dozen or more li before at last reaching the mountains. The mountain peaks rose graceful and lofty, and its streams and ravines ran clear. While Yan Qing admired the mountain scenery, evening stole upon them unawares. They beheld:

p.src: This mountain was called Mount Dapi. In high antiquity, the sage Yu the Great came here while channeling the Yellow River. The Book of Documents says, “He came to Dapi.” This is the proof of it. Today it lies within Jun County under Daming Prefecture. But let us waste no more words. Xu Guanzhong led Yan Qing around several mountain spurs and into a hollow, where an open, level tract extended three or four li in every direction. Two or three thatched cottages showed among the clustered trees. Among them stood several thatched rooms facing south beside a stream. A bamboo fence encircled the doorway, and the brushwood gate stood half closed; tall bamboo, dark pines, scarlet maples, and green cypresses grew densely before and behind. Xu Guanzhong pointed and said, “This is my snail’s dwelling.” Inside the bamboo fence, Yan Qing saw a yellow-haired country lad in a padded homespun jacket gathering dried pine branches and stumps from the ground and stacking them beneath the thatched eaves. Hearing hoofbeats, he stood and looked outside, crying in astonishment, “How can there be horses passing through here?” Looking closely, however, he saw that the rider behind was his master. He hurried out through the gate, stood with hands folded, and stared blankly. When the horses were being prepared before their departure, Xu Guanzhong had said that no bridle bells were needed; thus the boy noticed them only when they were close at hand. The two dismounted and entered through the bamboo fence. The soldier tethered the horses. The two entered the thatched hall and took their seats as host and guest. u.src: This mountain was called Mount Dapi. In high antiquity, the sage Yu the Great came here while channeling the Yellow River.
The Book of Documents says, “He came to Dapi.”
This is the proof of it.

u.src: Today it lies within Jun County under Daming Prefecture.
But let us waste no more words.
Xu Guanzhong led Yan Qing around several mountain spurs and into a hollow, where an open, level tract extended three or four li in every direction.
Two or three thatched cottages showed among the clustered trees.
Among them stood several thatched rooms facing south beside a stream.
A bamboo fence encircled the doorway, and the brushwood gate stood half closed; tall bamboo, dark pines, scarlet maples, and green cypresses grew densely before and behind.
Xu Guanzhong pointed and said, “This is my snail’s dwelling.”
Inside the bamboo fence, Yan Qing saw a yellow-haired country lad in a padded homespun jacket gathering dried pine branches and stumps from the ground and stacking them beneath the thatched eaves.
Hearing hoofbeats, he stood and looked outside, crying in astonishment, “How can there be horses passing through here?”
Looking closely, however, he saw that the rider behind was his master.
He hurried out through the gate, stood with hands folded, and stared blankly.
When the horses were being prepared before their departure, Xu Guanzhong had said that no bridle bells were needed; thus the boy noticed them only when they were close at hand.
The two dismounted and entered through the bamboo fence.
The soldier tethered the horses.
The two entered the thatched hall and took their seats as host and guest.

After tea, Guanzhong ordered the accompanying soldier to remove the saddles and bridles, lead the two horses to the thatched shed at the rear, and ask the boy to find fodder for them. He then told the soldier to rest in the side room at the front.
Yan Qing also went to pay his respects to Guanzhong’s aged mother.
Guanzhong then took Yan Qing to a thatched study on the eastern side, facing west.
Opening the rear window, they found it overlooking a clear stream, and the two sat leaning against the window rail.

p.src: Guan Zhong said, “My humble cottage is cramped and shabby; please do not laugh at it, brother!” Yan Qing replied, “With such lovely mountains and clear waters, I scarcely know where to look first. This is truly a rare place.” Guan Zhong then asked him about the campaign against Liao. After they had talked for some time, the boy came in and lit the lamps, closed the lattice windows, brought over a table, and set out five or six dishes of vegetables. He also brought a platter of chicken, a platter of fish, and two kinds of mountain fruit stored in the house, then warmed a pot of wine. Guan Zhong poured a cup, handed it to Yan Qing, and said, “I invited you here especially, brother, yet all I have to offer is rustic wine and country fare. How can this be fit for a guest?” Yan Qing thanked him, saying, “I ought not to have put you to such trouble.” After several cups of wine, moonlight shone outside the window as bright as day. When Yan Qing pushed open the window and looked out, he found another scene of equal purity and charm. The clouds were thin and the wind was still; the moon shone white and the stream ran clear, while reflections on the water and light upon the hills illumined the whole room together. Yan Qing praised the scene without end, saying, “In the old days at Daming Prefecture, there was no one with whom I was more intimate than you, brother. But ever since you sat the military examination, I have had no chance to see you. And now you have found such a splendid retreat—how secluded and elegant it is! As for a poor fellow like me, forever campaigning east and west, when shall I ever enjoy a single day of leisure?” Guan Zhong laughed and said, “Song Gongming and all the generals are heroes unmatched in the world, answering to the Stars of the Dipper in heaven, and now you have also subdued a powerful enemy by your might. How could one such as Xu, hiding like a snail in these barren hills, compare in the slightest with any of you? Moreover, I have always been somewhat out of step with the times. Whenever I see treacherous cliques monopolizing power and deceiving the court, I lose all desire for advancement. I have wandered over rivers and lakes and visited a number of places, observing affairs everywhere with considerable care.” When he had finished, he laughed heartily, rinsed the cups, and poured more wine. Yan Qing took out twenty taels of silver and offered them to Guan Zhong, saying, “This trifling gift is but a small token of my regard.” Guan Zhong firmly refused to accept it. Yan Qing then urged him, “With your talents and strategy, brother, you should come with me to the capital, watch for a suitable opportunity, and win yourself an official career.” Guan Zhong sighed and said, “Now that wicked men rule the day, envying the worthy and resenting the able, those who are like ghosts and demons all wear lofty caps and broad official sashes; while the loyal, good, and upright are all ensnared and ruined. My ambitions have long since turned to ashes. When you have achieved success and won renown, brother, you too would do well to seek a way of retreat. As the old saying goes, ‘When the birds are all brought down, the fine bow is put away.’” Yan Qing nodded and sighed. The two talked until midnight before at last retiring to rest.

p.src: Early the next morning, after they had washed, breakfast was promptly laid out. When Yan Qing had eaten, Guan Zhong invited him to ramble about the front and rear slopes of the mountain. Yan Qing climbed to a height and gazed into the distance. Range upon range rose in overlapping barriers, with mountains on every side. Only the cries of birds sounded high and low, and not a single traveler came or went. Even counting every household scattered through the mountains, there were only a little over twenty. Yan Qing said, “This place surpasses even the Peach Blossom Spring.” Yan Qing was so absorbed in admiring the mountain scenery that evening fell, and he stayed another night.

p.src: The next day, Yan Qing took leave of Guan Zhong, saying, “Commander Song may be worrying about me, so I must bid you farewell here.” Guan Zhong accompanied him out through the gate. Guan Zhong said, “Wait a moment, brother!” Before long, a village boy came out carrying a handscroll. Guan Zhong took it and handed it to Yan Qing, saying, “These are a few clumsy pictures I painted recently. When you reach the capital, brother, examine it carefully. It may perhaps prove useful someday.” Yan Qing thanked him and ordered a soldier to tie it securely inside his baggage. Neither could bear to part, and they walked on together for another mile or two. Yan Qing said, “‘Though one escorts a friend a thousand miles, the parting must come at last.’ There is no need to trouble yourself by coming farther. Let us hope to meet again.” The two parted, each heavy at heart.

p.src: Yan Qing watched until Xu Guanzhong had gone far on his way back, and only then mounted his horse. He ordered the soldiers to mount as well, and they all set out together. In little more than a day they reached the Eastern Capital. As it happened, Commander Song had stationed his troops at Chenqiao Post Station to await the imperial decree. Yan Qing entered the camp and reported himself; no more need be said of this.

p.src: Now earlier, Grand Commandant Su and Privy Councillor Zhao had led the central army into the city and reported Song Jiang and his men’s achievements to the Son of Heaven. They reported that Commander Song, his generals, and their troops had returned in triumph and had already reached the outskirts of the passes. Privy Councillor Zhao came forward and memorialized the hardships Song Jiang and the other generals had endured on the frontier. On hearing the memorial, the Son of Heaven praised them highly and at once issued an imperial decree, ordering an imperial chamberlain to summon Song Jiang and the others to an audience. All were to enter the city in full armor. Song Jiang and all the generals obeyed the imperial decree. Fully accoutred in military dress and leather belts, with helmets on their heads and armor on their bodies, they wore brocade coats and displayed their gold and silver badges. Entering through the Donghua Gate, they proceeded to the Wende Hall for an audience with the Son of Heaven, where they bowed, performed the ceremonial dance of homage, offered greetings, and cried “Long live the Emperor!” three times. The Emperor looked upon Song Jiang and the heroic generals. All wore brocade robes and golden belts, except Wu Yong, Gongsun Sheng, Lu Zhishen, and Wu Song, who retained their customary dress. The Son of Heaven was greatly delighted and said, “I am well aware, my lords, of the hardships you endured on campaign and of your devoted service at the frontier. Many of you were wounded, and I have been deeply grieved and anxious.” Song Jiang bowed twice and memorialized, “Through Your Majesty’s boundless fortune, as vast as heaven, although some among us were wounded, all are now safe and well. Now the rebel enemy has submitted and peace has returned to the frontier. This was truly brought about by Your Majesty’s awe-inspiring virtue; what hardship can we claim to have endured?” He bowed twice again and gave thanks. The Son of Heaven specially ordered the officials of the ministries and courts to deliberate upon ranks and titles for them. Grand Preceptor Cai Jing and Military Commissioner Tong Guan conferred and memorialized, “Allow us to deliberate upon official ranks and titles for Song Jiang and the others, and then report our proposals to Your Majesty.” The Son of Heaven approved their memorial. He further commanded the Court of Imperial Entertainments to prepare a grand imperial banquet and graciously awarded Song Jiang a brocade robe, a suit of golden armor, and a famed horse. Lu Junyi and all those below him were rewarded with gold and silk, to be issued entirely from the imperial treasury. After Song Jiang and the generals had given thanks for the imperial favor, they all left the palace precincts, went out beyond the Xihua Gate, mounted their horses, and returned to camp to rest and await the imperial decree. Several days passed before they knew it, yet Cai Jing, Tong Guan, and the rest did not deliberate upon any ranks or titles at all; they merely kept delaying the matter.

p.src: Now Song Jiang was sitting at leisure in camp, discussing with his strategist Wu Yong the rise and fall of states through the ages and the causes of their success and failure, when Dai Zong and Shi Xiu appeared, each dressed in plain clothes, and reported, “We have been sitting idle in camp with nothing to do, so today Brother Shi Xiu and I mean to take a stroll. We have come especially to inform you, elder brother.” Song Jiang said, “Come back to camp early. I shall wait for you, and we will drink a few cups together.” Dai Zong and Shi Xiu left the Chenqiao post station and strolled slowly northward. After passing through several streets and marketplaces, they suddenly saw a great stone stele beside the road. On it were the three characters “Terrace of the Creation of Writing,” with several lines of smaller characters above them, but these had been weathered by wind and rain and were no longer clearly legible. Dai Zong examined it carefully and said, “So this is where Cangjie created writing.” Shi Xiu laughed and said, “We have no use for him.” The two laughed and continued onward. They came to a place where a broad expanse of open ground lay covered with broken tiles and rubble. To the north stood a stone archway, with a horizontal slab engraved with the three characters “Bolang City.” Dai Zong pondered for a moment, then said, “So this is where the Marquis of Liu attempted to strike down the First Emperor of Qin.” Dai Zong clicked his tongue in admiration and exclaimed, “What a man the Marquis of Liu was!” Shi Xiu said, “A pity that blow missed its mark!” After lamenting this for a while, the two talked as they continued northward until they were more than twenty li from camp. Shi Xiu said, “We have fooled around for half the day. Let us find somewhere to drink a bowl of wine before returning to camp.” Dai Zong said, “Is that not a tavern up ahead?” The two entered the tavern and chose a bright seat by the window. Dai Zong rapped on the table and called, “Bring us wine!” The waiter brought five or six small dishes of vegetables, set them on the table, and asked, “How much wine would you gentlemen like?” Shi Xiu said, “Bring us two horns of wine first, and whatever good food you have to go with it—just keep it coming.” Before long, the waiter had warmed two horns of wine and brought a plate of beef, a plate of mutton, and a plate of tender chicken. As the two drank and chatted, they saw a man enter carrying an umbrella and staff, with a bundle on his back. His black gown was tucked up, a money pouch was tied at his waist, his knees were bound with guards, and he wore hemp sandals. He had walked so hard that he was gasping for breath. Once through the door, he put down his umbrella, staff, and bundle, seated himself, and called, “Quickly, bring me some wine and meat!” The waiter promptly warmed a horn of wine and set down two or three small dishes of vegetables. The man said, “No need for these dainty niceties. If you have meat, hurry and slice me a plate. Once I have eaten, I must press on into the city on official business.” He picked up the wine and drank in great gulps. Dai Zong watched him and thought to himself, “That fellow is a government runner. What damned business can he be on?” He cupped his hands toward the man and asked, “Brother, what matter is so urgent?” While eating and drinking, the man gave a muddled account in a few disjointed phrases. As a result, Song Gongming was to perform another extraordinary feat, and the lands of Fen and Qin were to return once more to the Great Song. But what did the man say? Listen to the explanation in the next chapter.
